import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Map 'has_video_4k' to more descriptive labels for better legend readability
df['has_video_4k_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'})

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a boxplot to visualize camera price distribution
# Grouped by sensor type and further broken down by 4K video capability
sns.boxplot(
    data=df,
    x='sensor_type',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='has_video_4k_label',
    palette='viridis', # Choose a color palette for visual appeal
    linewidth=0.8,
    flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=4, linestyle='none', alpha=0.6) # Style outliers
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels to prevent overlap and improve readability, especially if many categories
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a legend to explain the hue variable, placing it outside the plot area
plt.legend(title='4K Video Capability', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for better readability of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
